transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. As we all know, we have a preliminary-injunction hearing in three weeks, and I need to approve our response strategy before the motion papers are finalized. Before I sign off on anything, I need each of you to put your cards on the table. I want to hear about any material evidence we have or anticipate, any business constraints I should be aware of, and any proposed filing commitments or deadlines you think we need to meet. Let's go around the room. Who wants to start?

transcript.text: Here's what I found, Marisol. In the forensic image delivered after the strategy-memo cutoff, I located the former employee's signed confidentiality agreement, which we didn't previously have in our exhibit set. More critically, the logs show that 4,800 files — including source code and deployment scripts — were copied to an external drive. This is far more substantial than the general allegations we've been working from. These supplemental findings have not yet been added to the motion outline. Given the volume and specificity of what was taken, I recommend two things: first, we file a supplemental-evidence submission to get the signed agreement and the file-transfer logs in front of the court; and second, we include a request for an expedited forensic inspection of the competitor's systems in the injunction motion. The 4,800-file scope and the deployment scripts strongly suggest the code wasn't just taken — it was likely operationalized, and we need to confirm whether the competitor's hosted product is actually running on it. This also ties into Nadia's constraint: if we're carving out a 30-day transition period, the forensic inspection becomes even more important because we need to understand the extent of the competitor's use during that window and ensure the transition doesn't become a vehicle for further misappropriation.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Ethan, those findings are very strong, and I agree the forensic inspection request aligns well with the client's transition-period constraint. From the client's perspective, here's what I need us to think through: the 30-day carveout means the competitor's hosted product stays live for existing customers during that window, so we need to be clear in the motion papers that the carveout applies only to existing customers — not new customer acquisition. The client will want to see language that prevents the competitor from onboarding new users during the transition period while still allowing existing customers to be migrated off without service disruption. Also, if we're requesting an expedited forensic inspection during that same 30-day window, I'll need to flag that to the client — they'll want to understand the scope and timing of that inspection before we commit to it in the filing. Marisol, can we make sure the motion papers explicitly distinguish between the transition carveout for existing customers and a full shutdown as to everything else?

transcript.text:
Excellent work, both of you. This is exactly the kind of transparency I needed before approving strategy. Let me synthesize what I'm hearing and make some decisions.

First, on Nadia's constraint — yes, the motion papers will explicitly distinguish between the transition carveout for existing customers and a full shutdown as to everything else. The carveout applies only to existing customers; the competitor may not onboard new users during the transition period. I want that language drafted clearly so there's no ambiguity.

Second, on Ethan's findings — the signed confidentiality agreement and the 4,800-file transfer logs are exactly the kind of concrete evidence we need. I'm approving the supplemental-evidence submission to get those in front of the court. I'm also approving the expedited forensic inspection request, but I want the scope and timing coordinated with the 30-day transition window so the inspection doesn't disrupt existing customer service and the client understands what we're committing to.

Now, before I formalize this into a strategy approval, I want to make sure we're not missing anything else. Are there any other material evidence, business constraints, or filing commitments anyone needs to put on the table? I'd rather hear it now than discover it after the papers are finalized. If there's nothing else, I'll move to approve the strategy with these parameters.
